name: telegram-call
author: Keith Yeung
description: Synthesizes spoken audio from text via a local Kokoro-FastAPI server and places a 1-on-1 Telegram voice call that plays it. Self-installs and self-authenticates on first use; auth has a dedicated verification tool so a wrong code can be retried without invalidating it.

tools.name: synthesize_speech
tools.description: Convert a text message into an mp3 audio file using a local Kokoro-FastAPI server (default http://localhost:8880, override via KOKORO_URL env). Returns the absolute path of the generated audio file. Use this whenever the user asks to call someone with a spoken message rather than a pre-recorded file (e.g. 'call @alice about a possible gas leak'): first call this tool with the spoken text, then pass the returned path to `make_call` as `audio_path`. Results are cached by (voice, speed, text) hash so calling twice with the same args is free.

text.description: The message to speak. Should be a complete, natural-sounding spoken message — write it the way you'd say it out loud. Example: 'Hi Alice, this is an automated alert. There may be a gas leak in your house. Please check immediately and call emergency services if you smell gas.'

voice.description: Optional Kokoro voice name (e.g. 'af_heart', 'af_bella', 'af_nova', 'am_michael', 'bf_emma', 'bm_george'). Defaults to 'af_heart' or the KOKORO_VOICE env var.

speed.description: Optional speech rate multiplier (1.0 = normal, 0.5 = slow, 1.5 = fast). Defaults to 1.0.

tools.name: verify_telegram_code
tools.description: Submit a Telegram verification code (or 2FA cloud password) during the one-time login flow, OR ask Telegram to redeliver the current code via the next channel. ONLY use this AFTER `make_call` returned a message asking for a code/password — never as the first step. Where the code comes from: by default Telegram delivers the login code as an in-app message from the official 'Telegram' service-account chat to the user's existing logged-in sessions (phone app, Telegram Desktop, etc.); SMS / voice-call delivery only happens after `resend`. The tool's success message tells you which channel was used. Behaviour: (a) call with `code` to verify a code; (b) call with `password` to submit a 2FA cloud password; (c) call with `resend: true` if the user genuinely did not receive any code — Telegram will redeliver via the next available channel (typically APP → SMS → CALL). If Telegram rejects a code as invalid (typo) the auth state is preserved so you can retry with a corrected value; do NOT call `make_call` with `phone` again, that would force a new send_code and invalidate the current code. After successful verification you can call `make_call` to place the actual call.

code.description: The verification code Telegram sent to the user (typically 5 digits, no spaces or dashes). Provide this when `make_call` returned a 'verification code was sent' message.

password.description: The user's Telegram 2FA cloud password. Provide this when verification returned a '2FA enabled' message asking for `password`.

resend.description: Set to true to ask Telegram to redeliver the verification code via the next channel (in-app → SMS → voice call). Use this ONLY if the user is sure they did not receive a code at all — not if they entered a wrong code (in that case just retry with the correct `code`). Do not combine with `code`/`password`.

tools.name: make_call
tools.description: Place a 1-on-1 Telegram voice call to a user, play an audio file, and hang up. The very first invocation transparently sets up Python dependencies (~30-90s) and walks the user through a one-time Telegram login. CRITICAL: `phone` and `target` are TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE. `target` is the RECIPIENT (whoever the user is calling) — typically a @username. `phone` is the CALLER'S OWN Telegram account (the user themselves), used only during one-time auth. NEVER copy a `target` value into `phone`; that would send a Telegram login code to the call recipient, which is wrong and a privacy issue. If you don't already know the user's own Telegram phone number from the conversation, ASK them for it explicitly — phrase the question so it's unambiguous it's THEIR number, not the recipient's. The login flow is: (a) call `make_call` with `phone` set to the USER'S OWN Telegram number to trigger a verification code (delivered as an in-app message to their existing Telegram sessions first; SMS / voice call is a fallback via the `verify_telegram_code` `resend` flag); (b) call the SEPARATE `verify_telegram_code` tool with the `code` (and `password` if 2FA is enabled) — DO NOT call `make_call` with `phone` again after a code has been sent or you will invalidate it; (c) once verification succeeds, call `make_call` again with `target` and `audio_path` to actually place the call. If the user asked you to convey a spoken message (no pre-recorded file given), first call `synthesize_speech` to turn the text into an mp3, then pass that path here as `audio_path`. If `target` is missing, ASK the user — do not invent one.

target.description: Who to call on Telegram — i.e. the RECIPIENT. NOT the same as `phone` (which is the caller's own account during one-time auth). Accepts @username, numeric user_id, or +phone_number (phone numbers only resolve if that user is already in the caller's Telegram contacts; prefer @username when in doubt). If the user has not specified a target, ASK them rather than guessing.

audio_path.description: Absolute path to the audio file to play during the call. Any format ffmpeg can decode is accepted (mp3, wav, ogg, m4a, opus, ...). Typically obtained by first calling `synthesize_speech` with the spoken text.

message.description: Human-readable description of the call, surfaced in the success/failure output.

phone.description: DO NOT COPY THIS FROM `target`. `phone` is the *caller's* own Telegram account number (the user's own phone), used ONLY during one-time login to receive a verification code. `target` is the *recipient* being called. They are different people. If the user has not explicitly told you their OWN Telegram number in this conversation, you do not have a value for `phone` yet — ask them, do not invent one and do not reuse `target`. Format: international country code, e.g. '+447700900000', no spaces. Only set this on the FIRST authentication step. After a code has been sent, use `verify_telegram_code` instead — do NOT include `phone` again. Once authenticated, leave `phone` empty on normal calls.
